messages:
kevin: Ran a perf run on staging to reproduce the latency tail we saw today — nvtx/nsys traces attached. seeing repeated small cudaMalloc/free bursts around request boundaries, ~20-40ms spikes every ~200ms. stack looks like pooling fallback.

maria: can you paste the nsys summary? curious if the spikes line up with kernel launches or allocation calls.

kevin: perf-bot posted the quick summary: 
perf-bot: nsys summary: total time 3m12s, 78% GPU compute, 6% cudaMalloc, 12% memcpy, repeated allocation hotspots at 0.2s intervals. link: https://perf/runs/1769123456

kevin: snippet from nsys timeline (condensed):
```
0.00s: kernel A (forward) 12ms
0.01s: kernel B (kv lookup) 1ms
0.02s: cudaMalloc 18ms 
0.04s: kernel C (compute) 10ms
... repeat pattern per request
```

sam: that cudaMalloc jump is the smoking gun. looks like our arena pool is sometimes exhausted and we fall back to cudaMalloc. does the workload produce many short-lived caches?

kevin: yes, small KV cache entries for short prompts, we shard per-request and free aggressively. pool footprint seems tuned down on this node (pool_max_bytes=1GB) to fit multiple tenants.

maria: two quick experiments: increase pool_max_bytes to 4GB and enable per-thread caches (arena_shards=8) OR enable a bump allocator for short-lived KV slices. Which is lower risk?

devon: bump allocator needs code change + validation. increasing pool_max_bytes is config-only and we can A/B with canary. propose: 1) canary a single host with pool_max_bytes=4GB and arena_shards=8 2) run same nsys trace for 30k requests 3) compare allocation count and cudaMalloc time.

kevin: did a dry run on a dev node with pool_max_bytes=4GB, arena_shards=8. Result: cudaMalloc time dropped to 0.8% of trace and tail latency P99 improved from 153ms -> 98ms. memory fragmentation still visible but stable.

maria: nice. can you share the allocation histogram?

kevin: allocation histogram (dev run):
- 0-1KB: 62%
- 1KB-16KB: 28%
- 16KB-256KB: 8%
- >256KB: 2%
This tells us most allocations are tiny, so allocator slabbing could help a lot.

sam: yeah tiny allocations mean pool slab sizes should favor 64B/256B/4KB bins. current arena used 1KB base which causes internal fragmentation for many 64B allocations.

maria: good call. For production canary, also enable pooling debug flags: POOL_LOG_ALLOC=1 and POOL_HEAP_STATS=1 so we can confirm no fallback. set a short TTL for per-request caches to avoid long-term growth.

devon: i'm going to roll a canary to a dedicated host and run perf-bot job with nsys + perfetto for flamegraphs. expected timeline: deploy in 15m, run 10k requests, post trace.

kevin: FYI i also instrumented kernel selection path: we had a check that probes free memory and selects a smaller kernel variant if free < threshold; that check itself allocates a temp buffer in the failure path. i removed the allocation and replaced with a deviceQuery syscall — should avoid the extra malloc on the decision path. small patch landed in PR #4123.

sam: excellent. that kind of accidental allocation on hot path is classic. +1 for deviceQuery approach.

perf-bot: canary run posted: run_id=1769123678, 10k requests, P99 latency 102ms, cudaMalloc share 0.9%, allocation fallback events: 3 (all in startup), fragmentation ratio: 1.12. perf links: nsys https://perf/runs/1769123678/nsys perfetto https://perf/runs/1769123678/trace

maria: results look great. next steps: (1) propagate pool_max_bytes change to fleet with staged rollout (2) update default arena_shards to 8 for inference tier (3) follow up with allocator tuning: add 64B bin and 256B bin, move base slab to 512B.

kevin: i'll write the canary run notes + command for reproducing:
```bash
# reproduce locally:
sudo perf-bot run --nsys --duration 300 --concurrency 8 --workload short-prompts --target-host canary1
# pool config snippet:
REDWOOD_POOL_MAX_BYTES=4294967296
REDWOOD_ARENA_SHARDS=8
REDWOOD_POOL_DEBUG=1
```

sam: also add a quick unit test that forces pool exhaustion and confirms we don't call cudaMalloc in the hot path.

devon: i'll coordinate rollout and make a runbook entry under eng-runtime/operations for the config flip and rollback criteria.

kevin: thanks all. i'll collect the traces and open a follow-up that records before/after flamegraphs and kernel timelines.

maria: :tada: nice win for tail latency.

sam: :thumbsup:
